A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same YOSO research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison. v6 retains Appendices A–G and adds Appendices H–I.

before.justification: v5 reports original CIFAR-10 generation experiments, text-to-image evaluations, component ablations, and qualitative application results in Tables 1–4 and Figures 1–8.

after.justification: v6 retains those original results and adds ImageNet-64, FFHQ-1024, and zero-shot COCO experiments in Tables 5–7, plus additional qualitative comparisons.

M1.justification: The self-cooperative adversarial objective, consistency regularization, decoupled schedulers, annealing, latent perceptual loss, discriminator, initialization, and quick adaptation remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 is identical. The added experiments use new configurations without revising the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Beyond v5's CIFAR-10 and text-to-image coverage, Appendix H adds training from scratch on ImageNet-64, high-resolution face generation on FFHQ-1024, and fine-tuning using COYO-700M plus internal data. These substantially broaden the represented training data and evaluation domains.

E2.justification: New comparisons include BigGAN-deep, StyleGAN-XL, and ADM in Table 5; Diffusion-GAN and Diffusion2GAN in Table 6; and StyleGAN-T, GigaGAN, and SwiftBrush in Table 7. Figure 9 adds PixArt-δ (LCM). Table 6's Diffusion-GAN, associated with Wang et al., is distinct from the DDGANs comparator already present in v5.

E3.justification: Appendix H adds EDM-based ImageNet training, FFHQ comparisons using DC-AE latents and a 33M-parameter DiT-S with shared pretrained generator initialization, and zero-shot COCO FID-30k, CLIP Score-30k, and latency evaluation. These supplement the retained HPS and COCO-5k evaluation. The COCO experiment explicitly retrains YOSO; it does not establish changes to the original experiments.

E4.justification: The existing ablations remain intact. Figure 11 adds a focused qualitative sensitivity analysis comparing MSE against latent perceptual losses using encoder, decoder, all-layer, and bottleneck features in two-step LCM. Figure 10 adds qualitative one-step versus four-step YOSO-LoRA comparisons, extending the existing quantitative sampling-step evidence.

E5.justification: The additions retain point-estimate and qualitative reporting. There is no added or revised reporting of repeated runs, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 retain their numerical results. New Tables 5–7 report YOSO FID 2.65 on ImageNet-64, FID 16.23 on FFHQ-1024, and COCO FID-30k 8.90 with CLIP Score-30k 0.31 and latency 0.09 seconds. Figures 9–11 add comparative outputs and feature-layer findings. These are newly reported results under added settings, rather than same-setting improvements over v5.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, objectives, Proposition 1, and Appendix C proof are retained. Removing the explicit multiplication symbol in Equation 3 is mathematically equivalent typesetting, not a theoretical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about stable one-step generation, mode coverage, training from scratch, efficient LoRA fine-tuning, and adaptation from 512 to 1024 resolution. The appended evidence does not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix H newly argues that zero-shot COCO FID can conflict with human preferences and should be interpreted cautiously. Appendix I interprets the feature-layer comparisons as supporting latent perceptual loss across different feature choices. The existing mechanism explanations and Appendix B limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v6 documents DC-AE latents, the 33M-parameter DiT-S backbone, and common pretrained initialization for the new FFHQ comparison. It removes Section 6.1's LoRA-specific batch-size-128 statement, while Appendix G.2's generic batch-size-256 statement already appears in both versions; an actual training change is therefore not established. Existing optimizer, EMA, learning-rate, and code-access information is otherwise retained.

R1.justification: References are added for DC-AE, COYO-700M, Diffusion-GAN, Diffusion2GAN, and Pick-a-Pic, while the Hill et al. cooperative-learning citation is removed. The two Luo 2024 entries correspond to the previously cited Energy-calibrated VAE work. The main related-work discussion and research positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order are largely preserved. v6 adds acknowledgments and Appendices H–I, updates publication and affiliation text, and makes small wording and heading corrections. There is no extensive rewriting or reorganization of the retained material.

P2.justification: v6 substantially expands the comparative displays with Tables 5–7 and Figures 9–11. Figure 10 combines reused one-step examples with additional four-step outputs. Existing comparison figures are reformatted, Figure 4's caption defines NFE, and surrounding material reflows; the original tables and figures remain present.

improvement.justification: The added ImageNet-64 and FFHQ-1024 experiments broaden empirical support beyond v5's CIFAR-10 training-from-scratch evidence, while COCO reporting and the feature-layer analysis provide useful additional checks. The gain is limited by sparse documentation of the new protocols and an overbroad ImageNet interpretation: Table 5 reports YOSO FID 2.65, behind StyleGAN-XL at 1.52, ADM at 2.07, and EDM at 1.36. Overall, the evidence strengthens the paper, but does not fully support the breadth of the added performance language.
